name: Bethnal Green Nature Reserve
summary: A nature reserve on a former WW2 bomb site in Bethnal Green, looked after since 1977 by local people, which calls itself a cultural institute for ecological research and community learning.

music.notes: Community classes such as Qi Gong, and a free weekly Forest Friday forest school for local children and families.

accessibility.notes: Paths are wood-chip, and some are narrow or uneven, which may be hard going for self-propelled wheelchairs. Bethnal Green tube has no step-free access; the reserve recommends Whitechapel instead. Email ahead with any access questions.

evidence.quote: The Bethnal Green Nature Reserve is a cultural institute focused on ecological research and community learning in the heart of East London.
This space is a WW2 bomb-site that has been cared for since 1977 by local residents, volunteers, staff, trustees
Forest Friday is a free, weekly forest school inviting local children and families to explore the wonders of nature right on your doorstep.
Our site is step-free and wheelchair accessible.
We have a very comfortable wheelchair accessible compost toilet
we do use wood-chip on our pathways, which may be difficult for a self-aided wheelchair
Some areas of the Nature Reserve have small pathways and uneven ground/surfaces
This station does not have step-free access.
We recommend Whitechapel Station (Elizabeth Line, District, and Overground), which is fully step-free
